summary: Iwao Shima was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Nagoya University from around 1970 to 1979 and held posts at Kanazawa University from around 1989 to 2007, serving as a professor from circa 1996.

Izumi Hoshi is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. She completed her undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo between circa 1987 and 1997, later serving as an assistant professor (1997) and director (2019–2023) at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami works in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and held a post at the University of Washington.

J. A. B. van Buitenen worked in Indology and philosophy, completing a doctorate under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (~1948–1953). He held posts at Deccan College (~1953–1956), Utrecht University (1959–1961), and the University of Chicago (from 1961).
J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who held posts at SOAS University of London and the University of Colombo, both attested in 1996.

J. Gordon Melton is a religious studies scholar educated at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).
J. M. E. McTaggart was a philosopher who studied at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from around 1897 to 1923.

J. Robert Oppenheimer studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, and learned under Arthur William Ryder in 1933. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Caltech, Cambridge, the Manhattan Project (~1942–1945), and the Institute for Advanced Study (~1947–1966).

J. Thomas Rimer is a Japanology scholar who studied at Princeton and Columbia. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1983), the University of Maryland, College Park (~1985–1989), the University of Pittsburgh (~1989–2008), and UCLA.

Jack Copeland is a philosopher who studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford, and the University of Oxford (~1975–1979). He held academic posts at the University of Canterbury starting in 1985 and at the University of Portsmouth.
Jack Goody was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at St Albans School and St John's College (~1938–1946). He later held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1954 to 1984.
Jack Laughlin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from McMaster University in 1999. He held a post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Grimm was a linguist who studied at the University of Marburg from around 1802 to 1806. He later held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and Frederick William University Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2013.
Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts as an assistant professor of religion at William & Mary and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Jacob P. Dalton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1996–2002) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., later holding posts at Yale (2005), SOAS (~2005–2008), and UC Berkeley (~2008).

Jacob Samuel Speyer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern (~1867–1872). He held posts at the University of Amsterdam, University of Groningen, and Leiden University (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Basel, Göttingen, Leipzig, and Oxford, learning under Theodor Benfey and Friedrich Nietzsche. He held posts at the University of Basel (1876–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).

Jacqueline I. Stone is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at SFSU and UCLA under William R. LaFleur, and served as a professor at Princeton University from 1990 to 2019.

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed doctoral research under Julius Lipner. Her post at the University of Manchester was attested in 2005.
